paragraphs.sourceText: Blame your worthless workdays on meeting recovery syndrome
paragraphs.translationZh: 将你毫无价值的工作日归咎于遇到恢复综合症

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Phyllis Hartman knows what it’s like to make one’s way through the depths of office meeting hell. Managers at one of her former human resources jobs arranged so many meetings that attendees would fall asleep at the table or intentionally arrive late. With hours of her day blocked up with unnecessary meetings, she was often forced to make up her work during overtime. “I was actually working more hours than I probably would have needed to get the work done,” says Hartman, who is founder and president of PGHR Consulting in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 菲利斯·哈特曼 (Phyllis Hartman) 深知在办公室会议地狱的深处摸索到底是什么感觉。她以前从事人力资源工作的经理安排了太多会议，以至于与会者会在桌子上睡着或故意迟到。由于每天的时间都被不必要的会议所占用，她经常被迫加班来弥补工作。 “实际上，我的工作时间比完成工作所需的时间还要多，”宾夕法尼亚州匹兹堡 PGHR 咨询公司的创始人兼总裁 Hartman 说。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) She isn’t alone in her frustration. Between 11 million and 55 million meetings are held each day in the United States, costing most organisations between 7% and 15% of their personnel budgets. Every week, employees spend about six hours in meetings, while the average manager meets for a staggering 23 hours.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 她并不是唯一一个感到沮丧的人。美国每天召开 1100 万到 5500 万次会议，大多数组织的人事预算花费在 7% 到 15% 之间。员工每周开会的时间约为 6 小时，而经理平均开会的时间高达 23 小时。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) And though experts agree that traditional meetings are essential for making certain decisions and developing strategy, some employees view them as one of the most unnecessary parts of the workday. The result is not only hundreds of billions of wasted dollars, but an annoyance of what organisational psychologists call “meeting recovery syndrome (MRS)”: time spent cooling off and regaining focus after a useless meeting. If you run to the office kitchen to get some relief with colleagues after a frustrating meeting, you’re likely experiencing meeting recovery syndrome.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 尽管专家们一致认为传统会议对于制定某些决策和制定战略至关重要，但一些员工认为它们是工作日中最不必要的部分之一。结果不仅浪费了数千亿美元，而且带来了组织心理学家所说的“会议恢复综合症（MRS）”的烦恼：在一场无用的会议之后，需要花时间冷静下来并重新集中注意力。如果您在一次令人沮丧的会议后跑到办公室厨房与同事一起放松一下，您可能正在经历会议恢复综合症。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Meeting recovery syndrome is a concept that should be familiar to almost anyone who has held a formal job. It isn’t ground-breaking to say workers feel fatigued after a meeting, but only in recent decades have scientists deemed the condition worthy of further investigation. With its links to organisational efficiency and employee wellbeing, MRS has attracted the attention of psychologists aware of the need to understand its precise causes and cures.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 遇到恢复综合症是一个几乎所有从事过正式工作的人都应该熟悉的概念。说员工在会议后感到疲劳的说法并不具有开创性，但直到最近几十年，科学家才认为这种情况值得进一步研究。由于与组织效率和员工福祉相关，MRS 引起了心理学家的注意，他们意识到需要了解其确切原因和治疗方法。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Today, in so far as researchers can hypothesise, MRS is most easily understood as a slow renewal of finite mental and physical resources. When an employee sits through an ineffective meeting their brain power is essentially being drained away. Meetings drain vitality if they last too long, fail to engage employees or turn into one-sided lectures. The conservation of resources theory, originally proposed in 1989 by Dr Stevan Hobfoll, states that psychological stress occurs when a person’s resources are threatened or lost. When resources are low, a person will shift into defence to conserve their remaining supply. In the case of office meetings, where some of employees’ most valuable resources are their focus, alertness and motivation, this can mean an abrupt halt in productivity as they take time to recover.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 如今，就研究人员的假设而言，MRS 最容易被理解为有限精神和体力资源的缓慢更新。当员工坐在一场无效的会议上时，他们的脑力基本上就被耗尽了。如果会议持续时间太长、无法吸引员工或变成片面的讲座，就会耗尽活力。资源守恒理论最初由 Stevan Hobfoll 博士于 1989 年提出，指出当一个人的资源受到威胁或丧失时，就会产生心理压力。当资源不足时，人们会转入防御以保存剩余的供应。就办公室会议而言，员工最宝贵的资源是他们的注意力、警觉性和积极性，这可能意味着生产力突然停止，因为他们需要时间来恢复。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) As humans, when we transition from one task to another on the job — say from sitting in a meeting to doing normal work — it takes an effortful cognitive switch. We must detach ourselves from the previous task and expend significant mental energy to move on. If we are already drained to dangerous levels, then making the mental switch to the next thing is extra tough. It’s common to see people cyber-loafing after a frustrating meeting, going and getting coffee, interrupting a colleague and telling them about the meeting, and so on.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 作为人类，当我们在工作中从一项任务过渡到另一项任务时——比如从参加会议到做正常工作——需要付出努力的认知转换。我们必须把自己从之前的任务中抽离出来，花费大量的精力继续前进。如果我们已经精疲力竭到危险的程度，那么将精神转向下一件事情就格外困难。人们在一次令人沮丧的会议后上网闲逛、去喝杯咖啡、打断同事并告诉他们会议的情况等等是很常见的。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Each person’s ability to recover from horrible meetings is different. Some can bounce back quickly, while others carry their fatigue until the end of the workday. Yet while no formal MRS studies are currently underway, one can loosely speculate on the length of an average employee’s lag time. Switching tasks in a non-MRS condition takes about 10 to 15 minutes. With MRS, it may take as long as 45 minutes on average. It’s even worse when a worker has several meetings that are separated by 30 minutes. “Not enough time to transition in a non-MRS situation to get anything done, and in an MRS situation, not quite enough time to recover for the next meeting,” says researcher Joseph Allen. “Then, add the compounding of back-to-back bad meetings and we may have an epidemic on our hands.”
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 每个人从糟糕的会议中恢复的能力是不同的。有些人可以很快恢复，而另一些人则带着疲劳直到工作日结束。然而，虽然目前还没有正式的 MRS 研究正在进行，但人们可以粗略地推测一名员工平均滞后时间的长度。非MRS条件下切换任务大约需要10到15分钟。对于 MRS，平均可能需要长达 45 分钟。如果员工要召开多次会议，每次会议的间隔时间为 30 分钟，情况会更糟。 “在非 MRS 情况下，没有足够的时间来完成任何事情，而在 MRS 情况下，则没有足够的时间恢复到下一次会议，”研究员约瑟夫·艾伦 (Joseph Allen) 说。 “然后，再加上连续两场糟糕的会议，我们可能会面临一场流行病。”

paragraphs.sourceText: H) In an effort to combat the side effects of MRS, Allen, along with researcher Joseph Mroz and colleagues at the University of Nebraska-Omaha, published a study detailing the best ways to avoid common traps, including a concise checklist of do’s and don’ts applicable to any workplace. Drawing from around 200 papers to compile their comprehensive list, Mroz and his team may now hold a remedy to the largely undefined problem of MRS.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 为了对抗 MRS 的副作用，Allen 与内布拉斯加大学奥马哈分校的研究员 Joseph Mroz 及其同事发表了一项研究，详细介绍了避免常见陷阱的最佳方法，包括适用于任何工作场所的简要清单。 Mroz 和他的团队根据大约 200 篇论文编制了综合清单，现在可能找到了解决 MRS 很大程度上未定义问题的方法。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Mroz says a good place to start is asking ourselves if our meetings are even necessary in the first place. If all that’s on the agenda is a quick catch-up, or some non-urgent information sharing, it may better suit the group to send around an email instead. “The second thing I would always recommend is keep the meeting as small as possible,” says Mroz. “If they don’t actually have some kind of immediate input, then they can follow up later. They don’t need to be sitting in this hour-long meeting.” Less time in meetings would ultimately lead to more employee engagement in the meetings they do attend, which experts agree is a proven remedy for MRS.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) Mroz 说，一个好的起点是首先问问自己我们的会议是否有必要。如果议程上的所有内容都是快速跟进或一些非紧急信息共享，则可能更适合小组发送电子邮件。 “我始终建议的第二件事是会议规模尽可能小，”姆罗兹说。 “如果他们实际上没有立即得到某种意见，那么他们可以稍后跟进。他们不需要参加这个长达一小时的会议。”减少会议时间最终会提高员工对所参加会议的参与度，专家们认为这是针对 MRS 的行之有效的补救措施。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Employees also feel taxed when they are invited together to meetings that don’t inspire participation, says Cliff Scott, professor of organisational science. It takes precious time for them to vent their emotions, complain and try to regain focus after a pointless meeting — one of the main traps of MRS. Over time as employees find themselves tied up in more and more unnecessary meetings — and thus dealing with increasing lag times from MRS — the waste of workday hours can feel insulting.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 组织学教授克里夫·斯科特 (Cliff Scott) 表示，当员工被邀请一起参加不能激发参与的会议时，他们也会感到负担重。在一场毫无意义的会议之后，他们需要宝贵的时间来发泄情绪、抱怨并试图重新集中注意力——这是 MRS 的主要陷阱之一。随着时间的推移，员工发现自己被困在越来越多不必要的会议中，因此要应对 MRS 带来的越来越多的滞后时间，浪费工作日时间可能会让人感到侮辱。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Despite the relative scarcity of research behind the subject, Hartman has taught herself many of the same tricks suggested in Mroz’s study, and has come a long way since her days of being stuck with unnecessary meetings. The people she invites to meetings today include not just the essential employees, but also representatives from every department that might have a stake in the issue at hand. Managers like her, who seek input even from non-experts to shape their decisions, can find greater support and cooperation from their workforce, she says.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 尽管这个主题背后的研究相对匮乏，哈特曼还是自学了许多在莫罗兹的研究中提出的相同技巧，并且自从她被困在不必要的会议中以来已经取得了很大的进步。她今天邀请参加会议的人不仅包括重要员工，还包括可能与当前问题有利害关系的每个部门的代表。她说，像她这样的管理者甚至会寻求非专家的意见来制定决策，因此可以从员工那里找到更多的支持和合作。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) If an organisation were to apply all 22 suggestions from Mroz and Allen’s findings, the most noticeable difference would be a stark decrease in the total number of meetings on the schedule, Mroz says. Less time in meetings would ultimately lead to increased productivity, which is the ultimate objective of convening a meeting. While none of the counter-MRS ideas have been tested empirically yet, Allen says one trick with promise is for employees to identify things that quickly change their mood from negative to positive. As simple as it sounds, finding a personal happy place, going there and then coming straight back to work might be key to facilitating recovery.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) Mroz 说，如果一个组织应用 Mroz 和 Allen 调查结果中的全部 22 条建议，最明显的区别将是日程安排上的会议总数明显减少。减少会议时间最终会提高生产力，这是召开会议的最终目标。艾伦表示，尽管尚未对任何反 MRS 的想法进行过实证检验，但有一个有希望的技巧是让员工找出能够迅速将他们的情绪从消极转变为积极的事物。听起来很简单，找到一个个人快乐的地方，去那里然后直接回去工作可能是促进康复的关键。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Leaders should see also themselves as “stewards of everyone else’s valuable time”, adds Steven Rogelberg, author of The Surprising Science of Meetings. Having the skills to foresee potential traps and treat employees’ endurance with care allows leaders to provide effective short-term deterrents to MRS.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 《会议的惊人科学》一书的作者史蒂文·罗格尔伯格补充道，领导者还应该将自己视为“其他人宝贵时间的管理者”。领导者如果有能力预见潜在的陷阱并谨慎对待员工的耐力，就可以对 MRS 提供有效的短期威慑。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Most important, however, is for organisations to awaken to the concept of meetings being flexible, says Allen. By reshaping the way they prioritise employees’ time, companies can eliminate the very sources of MRS in their tracks.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 然而，最重要的是让组织意识到会议灵活的概念，艾伦说。通过重塑员工时间的优先顺序，公司可以消除 MRS 的根源。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Although employees are said to be fatigued by meetings, the condition has not been considered worthy of further research until recently.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 虽然据说员工因会议而感到疲劳，但直到最近才认为这种情况值得进一步研究。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Mroz and his team compiled a list of what to do and what not to do to remedy the problem of MRS.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. Mroz 和他的团队编制了一份清单，列出了解决 MRS 问题该做什么和不该做什么的清单。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Companies can get rid of the root cause of MRS if they give priority to workers’ time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 如果公司优先考虑工人的时间，就可以消除 MRS 的根源。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. If workers are exhausted to a dangerous degree, it is extremely hard for them to transition to the next task.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 如果工人精疲力尽到危险程度，他们就很难过渡到下一个任务。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Employees in America spend a lot of time attending meetings while the number of hours managers meet is several times more.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 美国员工花大量时间参加会议，而经理开会的时间是其数倍。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Phyllis Hartman has learned by herself many of the ways Mroz suggested in his study and made remarkable success in freeing herself from unnecessary meetings.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 菲利斯·哈特曼（Phyllis Hartman）自己学习了姆罗兹在研究中建议的许多方法，并在将自己从不必要的会议中解放出来方面取得了显着的成功。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. When meetings continue too long or don’t engage employees, they deplete vitality.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 当会议持续太长时间或没有员工参与时，就会耗尽活力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. When the time of meetings is reduced, employees will be more engaged in the meetings they do participate in.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 当会议时间减少时，员工会更加投入到他们参加的会议中。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Some employees consider meetings one of the most dispensable parts of the workday.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 一些员工认为会议是工作日中最可有可无的部分之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. According to Mroz, if all his suggestions were applied, a very obvious change would be a steep decrease in the number of meetings scheduled.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. Mroz 表示，如果他的所有建议都得到采纳，一个非常明显的变化将是安排的会议数量急剧减少。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common: You know them when you hear them. Sarcasm is mostly understood through tone of voice, which is used to portray the opposite of the literal words. For example, when someone says, “Well, that’s exactly what I need right now,” their tone can tell you it’s not what they need at all.
paragraphs.translationZh: 讽刺和爵士乐有一些令人惊讶的共同点：当你听到它们时你就知道它们。讽刺主要是通过语气来理解的，语气用来描绘与字面意思相反的意思。例如，当有人说“嗯，这正是我现在需要的”时，他们的语气可以告诉你这根本不是他们需要的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Most frequently, sarcasm highlights an irritation or is, quite simply, mean.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最常见的情况是，讽刺凸显了一种恼怒，或者很简单，就是刻薄。

paragraphs.sourceText: If you want to be happier and improve your relationships, cut out sarcasm. Why? Because sarcasm is actually hostility disguised as humor.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果您想变得更快乐并改善人际关系，请停止讽刺。为什么？因为讽刺实际上是伪装成幽默的敌意。

paragraphs.sourceText: Despite smiling outwardly, many people who receive sarcastic comments feel put down and often think the sarcastic person is rude, or contemptible. Indeed, it’s not surprising that the origin of the word sarcasm derives from the Greek word “sarkazein” which literally means “to tear or strip the flesh off.” Hence, it’s no wonder that sarcasm is often preceded by the word “cutting” and that it hurts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管表面上微笑，但许多收到讽刺评论的人会感到沮丧，并常常认为讽刺的人很粗鲁或可鄙。事实上，讽刺这个词的起源源于希腊语“sarkazein”，字面意思是“撕下或剥掉肉体”，这并不奇怪。因此，毫不奇怪，讽刺前面经常出现“切割”这个词，这很伤人。

paragraphs.sourceText: What’s more, since actions strongly determine thoughts and feelings, when a person consistently acts sarcastically it may only serve to heighten their underlying hostility and insecurity. After all, when you come right down to it, sarcasm can be used as a subtle form of bullying — and most bullies are angry, insecure, or cowardly.
paragraphs.translationZh: 更重要的是，由于行为在很大程度上决定了思想和感受，当一个人持续表现出讽刺时，可能只会加剧他们潜在的敌意和不安全感。毕竟，归根结底，讽刺可以被用作一种微妙的欺凌形式——而且大多数欺凌者都是愤怒、缺乏安全感或胆怯的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Alternatively, when a person stops voicing negative comments, especially sarcastic ones, they may soon start to feel happier and more self-confident. Also, other people in their life benefit even more because they no longer have to hear the emotionally hurtful language of sarcasm.
paragraphs.translationZh: 或者，当一个人停止发表负面评论，尤其是讽刺性评论时，他们可能很快就会开始感到更快乐、更自信。此外，生活中的其他人也受益更多，因为他们不再需要听到伤人的讽刺语言。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now, I’m not saying all sarcasm is bad. It may just be better used sparingly — like a potent spice in cooking. Too much of the spice, and the dish will be overwhelmed by it. Similarly, an occasional dash of sarcastic wit can spice up a chat and add an element of humor to it. But a big or steady serving of sarcasm will overwhelm the emotional flavor of any conversation and can taste very bitter to its recipient.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，我并不是说所有讽刺都是不好的。它可能只是少量使用更好——就像烹饪中的强力香料一样。太多的香料，菜会被它淹没。同样，偶尔的讽刺可以让聊天变得有趣，并增添幽默的元素。但是大量或持续的讽刺会压倒任何谈话的情感味道，并且会给接受者带来非常痛苦的感觉。

paragraphs.sourceText: So, tone down the sarcasm and work on clever wit instead, which is usually without any hostility and thus more appreciated by those you’re communicating with. In essence, sarcasm is easy while true, harmless wit takes talent.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，请淡化讽刺，转而使用聪明的智慧，这通常没有任何敌意，因此更容易受到与你交流的人的赞赏。从本质上讲，讽刺很容易，而真实、无害的机智则需要天赋。

paragraphs.sourceText: Thus, the main difference between wit and sarcasm is that, as already stated, sarcasm is often hostility disguised as humor. It can be intended to hurt and is often bitter and biting. Witty statements are usually in response to someone’s unhelpful remarks or behaviors, and the intent is to untangle and clarify the issue by emphasizing its absurdities. Sarcastic statements are expressed in a cutting manner; witty remarks are delivered with undisguised and harmless humor.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，机智和讽刺之间的主要区别在于，如前所述，讽刺往往是伪装成幽默的敌意。它可能是为了伤害，而且常常是苦涩的。诙谐的言论通常是对某人无益的言论或行为的回应，其目的是通过强调问题的荒谬性来理清和澄清问题。讽刺性的言论以尖刻的方式表达；诙谐的言论以毫不掩饰和无害的幽默来表达。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Variability is crucially important for learning new skills. Consider learning how to serve in tennis. Should you always practise serving from the exactly same location on the court, aiming at the same spot? Although practising in more variable conditions will be slower at first, it will likely make you a better tennis player in the end. This is because variability leads to better generalisation of what is learned.
paragraphs.translationZh: 可变性对于学习新技能至关重要。考虑学习如何打网球发球。您是否应该始终在球场上的同一位置练习发球，瞄准同一位置？尽管在多变的条件下练习一开始会比较慢，但最终可能会让你成为一名更好的网球运动员。这是因为可变性可以更好地概括所学内容。

paragraphs.sourceText: This principle is found in many domains, including speech perception and learning categories. For instance, infants will struggle to learn the category “dog” if they are only exposed to Chihuahuas, instead of many different kinds of dogs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这一原则存在于许多领域，包括语音感知和学习类别。例如，如果婴儿只接触吉娃娃而不是许多不同种类的狗，他们将很难学习“狗”这一类别。

paragraphs.sourceText: “There are over ten different names for this basic principle,” says Limor Raviv, the senior investigator of a recent study. “Learning from less variable input is often fast, but may fail to generalise to new stimuli.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “这一基本原理有十多个不同的名称，”最近一项研究的高级研究员利莫尔·拉维夫 (Limor Raviv) 说。 “从变量较少的输入中学习通常很快，但可能无法推广到新的刺激。”

paragraphs.sourceText: To identify key patterns and understand the underlying principles of variability effects, Raviv and her colleagues reviewed over 150 studies on variability and generalisation across fields, including computer science, linguistics, categorisation, visual perception and formal education.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为了确定关键模式并了解变异性影响的基本原理，Raviv 和她的同事回顾了 150 多项跨领域的变异性和泛化研究，包括计算机科学、语言学、分类、视觉感知和正规教育。

paragraphs.sourceText: The researchers discovered that, across studies, the term variability can refer to at least four different kinds of variability, such as set size and scheduling. “These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared — which means that we currently don’t know which is most effective for learning,” says Raviv.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员发现，在研究中，术语“可变性”可以指至少四种不同类型的可变性，例如集合大小和调度。 “这四种变异性从未被直接比较过——这意味着我们目前不知道哪种对学习最有效，”拉维夫说。

paragraphs.sourceText: The impact of variability depends on whether it is relevant to the task or not. But according to the “Mr. Miyagi principle”, practising seemingly unrelated skills may actually benefit learning of other skills.
paragraphs.translationZh: 可变性的影响取决于它是否与任务相关。但根据“宫城先生原则”，练习看似无关的技能实际上可能有益于其他技能的学习。

paragraphs.sourceText: But why does variability impact learning and generalisation? One theory is that more variable input can highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但为什么变异性会影响学习和泛化呢？一种理论认为，更多的可变输入可以突出任务的哪些方面相关，哪些方面不相关。

paragraphs.sourceText: Another theory is that greater variability leads to broader generalisations. This is because variability will represent the real world better, including atypical (非典型的) examples.
paragraphs.translationZh: 另一种理论是，更大的可变性导致更广泛的概括。这是因为可变性将更好地代表现实世界，包括非典型的例子。

paragraphs.sourceText: A third reason has to do with the way memory works: when training is variable, learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第三个原因与记忆的工作方式有关：当训练发生变化时，学习者被迫主动重建他们的记忆。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Understanding the impact of variability is important for literally every aspect of our daily life. Beyond affecting the way we learn language, motor skills, and categories, it even has an impact on our social lives,” explains Raviv. “For example, face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community. Exposure to fewer faces during childhood is associated with diminished face memory.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “了解变异性的影响对于我们日常生活的各个方面都很重要。除了影响我们学习语言、运动技能和类别的方式之外，它甚至还会影响我们的社交生活，”拉维夫解释道。 “例如，人脸识别受到人们是在小社区还是在大社区长大的影响。童年时期接触较少的面孔与面孔记忆的减弱有关。”

paragraphs.sourceText: “We hope this work will spark people’s curiosity and generate more work on the topic,” concludes Raviv. “Our paper raises a lot of open questions. Can we find similar effects of variability beyond the brain, for instance, in the immune system?”
paragraphs.translationZh: 拉维夫总结道：“我们希望这项工作能够激发人们的好奇心，并在这个主题上产生更多的工作。” “我们的论文提出了很多悬而未决的问题。我们能否在大脑之外，例如在免疫系统中，找到类似的变异效应？”
